Separate reflection, foam and body-color views showed that reflected sky is responsible for much of the broad silver appearance; actual foam is more localized. A default-off optical extension for the added main channel is under rendered validation. It must preserve the original offshoot and upstream source optics.

Removing the full water composite also exposed white bank fringes and sky holes beside the waterfall in the opaque scene. Saved water-sheet arrays contained no tall triangles that explained those artifacts. The terrain and cliff junction, including normals beside removed heightfield faces, therefore needs its own correction. Internal cliff-mesh integrity alone does not verify its external terrain connections.

Fixed-time rendered comparisons confirm that the main-channel optical correction restores darker water and submerged detail. Independent review still rejects broad connected silver streaks. A later terrain closure candidate restored full heightfield faces, which hid the waterfall behind vertical walls despite passing standalone cliff-clearance checks. That candidate was rejected. Acceptance requires the combined terrain and cliff to leave the falling-water corridor visible, as well as closing external seams.

The next optical revision masks back-facing ripple facets and uses smaller current-aligned waves only inside the added main channel. The CPU floater sampler receives the same quantized ownership mask and wave phases. A fixed-time original calm-pool comparison showed no changed scene pixels with the extension enabled or disabled. Actual overhead GPU readback agreed with the CPU within 0.09 mm at two tested main-channel points, but differed by 2.29 mm at a third. A closer two-meter probe at all three points, enabled and disabled, reduced the largest difference to 0.017 mm. This supports formula parity at an unminified footprint; the more distant filtering difference remains a measured limitation. Those early wave-height checks covered optics and floaters rather than vertex displacement. They did not establish raised geometric crests or the visual reference bar. The later geometry check is described below.

The carried white-water field represents local coverage. The inherited shader expands moderate values through a nonlinear coverage curve. The added main channel now uses a bounded share of that field and smaller current-aligned foam aggregates. The measured expected share over 797 sampled main-channel cells falls from 12.8% to 6.8%, before contact and wake unions. Actual rendered review still rejects broad bright patches; diagnostic separation of reflection, body color and foam remains necessary. The ownership texture also follows edits to the original river's path, keeping that edited channel outside the main-only treatment.

The main channel's broad standing-wave band now also displaces actual triangles. Only affected faces receive local subdivision; the original reach keeps its geometry. On the current default fixture this adds 1,038 triangles. CPU floaters interpolate those same displaced triangles, and 7,451 centroid checks agree exactly. The first three close GPU readbacks differed by up to 0.654 mm. That diagnostic subtracted a filtered half-float flow level on the GPU and a CPU-interpolated level on the CPU. Using one shared constant height origin isolates actual triangle height: the same three close points now agree within 0.006 mm. This is a sampled check, not exhaustive GPU equality. Fine ripple bands remain optical. Mesh updates follow flow snapshots rather than a full CPU rebuild every animation frame.

The receiving pool also has a bounded vertical-impact wave approximation. Accepted landing discharge and vertical arrival speed set its energy; rejected inflow produces none. Two outward wave bands use 2.8 and 4.2 m wavelengths and fade by 8 m from impact. Their default-flow RMS is about 4.47 cm. CPU floaters interpolate the same time-varying vertex displacement, with 2,115 triangle samples agreeing within floating-point precision. This adds no solver mass or foam. A five-second close render shows moving surface deformation, and two close GPU samples agree with the floater surface within 0.0064 mm. The impact still fails visual review for its compact foam footprint and weak connected spray. It is not a solved three-dimensional impact circulation.

The pool-bank needles were traced to a terrain discontinuity, separately from a normal-map fault. One branch used the original bank coordinate while its neighbor blended valley height using the wandered bank coordinate. Both sides now use the same receiving-bank blend. Rendered inspection removes the large needles, and all 19 headwater tests pass, including a profile regression and independent blocked-landing recovery. A fresh width 1, depth 1, Q 1.5 fixture passed three balance windows after 180 simulated seconds, with zero restores and a mass residual of 1.96e-11 cubic meters. Mean outflow was 1.561 and storage loss 0.061 cubic meters per second. Numerical acceptance remains separate from realism: the latest rendered review still rejects the uniform waterfall ribbon, compact impact, stepped cliff and foil-like rapids highlights.

The airborne body uses a bounded swept volume around the shared ballistic trajectory. Its liquid fraction integrates to discharge divided by local speed; entrained air expands the optical envelope without adding solver water. Seeded three-dimensional density is advected through the fall. Shared geometry and inverse sampling preserve section area during deformation. Fine descending density replaced coarse clumps in round 22, but fresh visual review rejected its uniform strands and outline. Scattering, entrainment and turbulent shape remain calibrated approximations. The original river retains its existing surface material. Fewer ray samples and a shared lighting centroid reduce estimated texture work; actual compiled shader evidence was captured, but no isolated GPU-duration improvement is claimed.

The receiving pool and added rapids use a screen-edge refraction fallback toward the undistorted scene sample when the projected bed leaves the image. This prevents the last screen row from stretching into a false vertical surface. Fixed-time rendered on/off comparisons remove the visible artifact. The pool-only correction changed zero pixels in the original calm-pool view across 2,128,484 pixels; extending it to the added rapids also changed zero across 921,600 original-pool pixels. The original river and source reach retain their existing path. This is an optical correction, not a change to water volume.

The added main channel carries local surface forcing and microslope in the previously unused channels of its third flow texture. Both visible geometry and the CPU floater mirror consume those fields. Main-owned white-water generation now follows rock contact, downstream drops and compressive jumps through the existing transport and decay system. Optional `cellS` ownership travels with mapper initialization and bed patches; absent ownership preserves the legacy path. Thirty focused headwater and mapping tests pass. This does not introduce a second foam simulation. Rendered foam coverage still needs correction: round 22 foam isolation confirms broad foreground streaks even after source localization.

The round 22 high, default and narrow/deep low-flow fixtures each passed three balance windows after about 180 additional simulated seconds from checksummed prior fields, with zero restores and mass residuals below 6e-11 cubic meters. The low-flow harness first applied a shape edit after importing an already shaped field; that invalid warm start failed conservation and was discarded. Applying the requested shape before importing depths fixed the setup, without changing product equations. Instantaneous original-branch discharge remains only about 0.015 to 0.050 cubic meters per second in these runs, so branch-split calibration remains open. A fixed-time main-optics on/off comparison changed zero of 921,600 original-pool pixels. Three near-camera probes of actual displaced GPU triangles agreed with the floater mirror within 0.003308 mm. These are structural and preservation checks, not a realism pass.

The broad rapids drops were also rejected: three identical cuts spanned most of the channel while rock relocation removed its central obstacles. Unequal oblique cuts now leave lateral bypasses, and relocation is limited to their narrow mouths. The original downstream rock field remains unchanged; four central native obstacles remain between the chutes for the judged seed. All 23 focused headwater and profile tests pass. Three new fixtures with this bed passed three consecutive balance windows with zero restores and zero ceiling breaches: Q12 at width 1/depth 1 after 180 simulated seconds, Q1.5 at width 1/depth 1 after 480 seconds, and Q0.5 at width 0.6/depth 2 after 2580 seconds. The settled original offshoot carries only about 0.017 to 0.026 cubic meters per second in these fixtures; its physical and visual split remains an open calibration issue. Reflection, transmission and foam isolation show that high distributed roughness remains a major cause of the silvery rapids field. Positive offshoot flow alone is not evidence of a calibrated or visually adequate branch split.

Round 28 remains in progress and has no realism acceptance. The dry cliff support now reaches the face over a narrower shoulder, reducing the low-flow upper overhang from about 19.2 m to 3.15 m at the measured section. High- and low-flow renders still show repeated albedo patterns and smooth falling-water bands. An actual-triangle ray audit found ground support beneath all 455 sampled high-elevation vegetation instances in the side-camera scope. The apparent floating crowns came from distant canopy models without trunks. Optional stems now reuse those exact far-tree transforms within 160 m of the source crest above 30 m elevation; downstream placements and the random sequence stay unchanged. Four focused stem tests and scoped Scene/View types pass, and the added stems were inspected in the rendered high-flow mountain.

The round 28 optical probe runs the same GPU density and absorption expressions as the visible fall. Its padded Cartesian export is explicitly clipped to production bounds; the density function alone extends a small impact taper beyond those bounds. Coarse and refined sampling differ by about 6.4 percent in integrated liquid after clipping, so spatial convergence remains unresolved. A separate angular radiative-transfer prototype passes positivity and power accounting tests but has not passed angular refinement or rendered realism. It remains disconnected from the default material. A histogram-preserving rock-albedo helper is also isolated: the first two native GPU comparisons failed the declared RGB tolerances, despite focused CPU checks passing. Neither experiment is an accepted visual replacement.

Boundary-light worker batches now request 32 ms instead of 2 ms; the main-thread geometry-copy budget stays 2 ms. One native high-flow receipt observed about 6.58 s of worker CPU time, a 59.6 ms maximum worker slice and a 60.5 ms main-thread scan readback. These are observed costs, not hard scheduling guarantees or a controlled FPS improvement. The separate receiving-worker integration remains off by default while live edit and performance gates are pending.

The frozen round 28 angular-transport experiment was rendered with signed density/light inputs and shared sunlight disabled in both comparison frames. Its 8,320-cell, 12-direction diffuse solve reached residual 8.76e-7 and relative power error 5.99e-7 after 480 sweeps and about 34 seconds of CPU work. Side and close-body renders were rejected: the body became more uniformly white without believable turbulent breakup. The optional diagnostic source remains disabled by default. Moving the actual camera cleared the frozen source automatically. The inactive hook changed 795 of 921,600 compared side-view pixels, with maximum channel difference 4/255; it is not bit-exact parity. Numerical readiness does not establish spatial/angular convergence or visual realism.

The round 28 topology audit disproved strict cliff watertightness. The baseline and the proposed right buttress share 60, 60 and 63 internal boundary edges at width scales 0.75, 1 and 1.8. Their triangle indices and edge owners match, so the buttress adds no new seams, but forward rays through the small components miss both meshes. The subdivision routine discards clipped polygons below projected area 1e-6; the first confirmed missing domain has area 1.193e-7. Components span up to about 2.8 mm laterally and 11.7 mm vertically in the audited widths. GG-384 tracks this existing topology defect. Earlier descriptions of a closed core refer to the intended shell construction and do not establish watertightness.

The optional round 29 finite-sheet density profile remains disabled. Six tests preserve the legacy CPU snapshots exactly and bound the candidate sampled mass error at 0.123 percent with liquid fraction no greater than one. Developed support has no permanent transverse columns, but actual opacity and shaded renders still form a nearly uniform white ribbon with a squared notch. The reused independent critic rejected it. The candidate uses 129 age rows and 16 Hz snapshots, occupying 594,432 bytes. Native first activation took 713 ms and its initial snapshot work took 58.4 ms; lower CPU test costs are not live frame-time proof. The next morphology gate is varied projected optical depth through connected folds, rather than just changing the outer silhouette. All optical coefficients and the original river material remain unchanged.

The isolated stochastic-rock experiment now passes a native explicit-LOD 3.5 RGB check: p99 error 0.000279 and maximum 0.000644 against unchanged limits 0.003 and 0.015. The installed Three WebGPU backend ignores manually supplied DataTexture mip levels, so this helper uses native mip generation. A second defect came from globally cached shader functions capturing texture uniforms from the probe builder; texture-closing functions are now scoped to each builder and shader stage. Twelve focused tests pass. The actual implicit-LOD scene renders after both repairs and passes scoped GPU frame validation. This remains an isolated albedo experiment, without corresponding boundary-cache or native normal-map integration; it is not an accepted production material.

The optional round 30 connected-fold profile also remains disabled. Eight focused tests bound sampled liquid-volume error at 0.105 percent, including the accepted low-flow configuration, and show one connected developed support. Actual body, opacity, and side renders nevertheless form braided ropes with repeated large holes. The reused independent critic rejected this morphology. Native initialization took 1,188 ms and the initial two-snapshot update took 164.6 ms; the 257-row, 1.18 MB density texture is a frozen diagnostic with unaccepted live cost. Optical settings and the original river remain unchanged. A separate optional directional-sun transport contract passes 25 focused tests but has not yet passed native scene or visual acceptance; six entry-face visibility arrays alone cannot account for an opaque cliff embedded inside the transport box. The native HIGH export confirms this limitation: 3,970 actual indexed cliff triangles intersect the padded transport box. Coefficients were finite, but eligibility was false; no native solar solve or activation was performed. Correcting this requires internal opaque transport and power accounting, or a clearly limited diagnostic domain.

## Source surges and dry ground

The live river now accepts a temporary source hydrograph: a smooth rise, a hold, and a smooth recession. The preview defaults to a peak of 120 cubic meters per second for 180 simulation seconds. Pause also pauses the release. Ending the surge gradually restores normal source flow; it does not remove water already released. The worker delays pool injection by the captured waterfall flight time. Local shallow-water transport then changes downstream depth and speed as that water arrives. Normal flow and opening controls stay fixed while the released waterfall tail is in flight.

LiveRiver enables adaptive wet-front coverage for ordinary flow as well as floods. All fully dry remote cells can sleep, including the original design footprint. Wet cells, positive films, inlets, and a neighboring face margin remain active. Approaching water wakes eligible dry ground using the actual local water surface. The old design ceiling is not an inner flood wall. This still uses a finite 480 by 235 meter grid; automatic outer-domain growth and sparse memory allocation are not implemented. Rebuilding active row runs still scans the grid when coverage changes. A native cold-start measurement reduced active work from 88,161 to 186 cells after eight steps, with full-grid bookkeeping taking 1.15 to 2.48 ms. This is a dry-start measurement, not a steady river frame-time claim.

Eleven focused flood and solver tests cover source-only release, cancellation continuity, delayed arrival, overbank transport, conservation, stronger-source timesteps, sleeping original cells, reawakening, and state restoration. A dense comparison matched adaptive fields to twelve decimal places over 300 steps. A repeat on the final sleeping implementation confirmed that a native 120 cubic meter per second pulse put more than 1 cm of water into 709 cells outside the former ceiling: 177.25 square meters. The accounting residual was below 4e-11 cubic meters, with no top-ups or restores. Final rendered overflow acceptance remains pending.

The falling body follows emission history by section age instead of changing every section at once. The ordinary legacy atlas remains unchanged outside a pulse. Seven focused tests cover history, cancellation and section budgets; sampled section error stayed below 0.137 percent. This does not establish exact three-dimensional airborne volume: thick rotating crest sections can overlap, and invalid center-plane mappings use a bounded diagnostic fallback. The preview supports durations from 30 to 600 seconds. Warm transient atlas updates measured 7 to 19 ms; initial and skipped-time updates can hitch. The actual GPU renderer now compiles and isolated rendered captures at pulse times 0, 2, 5, 10 and 34 seconds show the upper body changing before the lower body, increasing launch distance and a return to normal after the tail. The receiving river field was frozen in this isolation check. A separate native preview check verified Start, Pause, Run and End surge: paused release held at normal flow, then source107.7 and accepted pool93.6 cubic meters per second showed the delay. Ending while paused kept both instantaneous rates unchanged and began a24-second recession/tail. Rendered overbank coverage is still not measured. First-frame compilation still took 65 to 72 seconds. Falling water remains too white and smooth for realism acceptance.

The split-color repair replaces a binary main-channel ownership switch with a short spatial transition on the main-channel side. The protected original channel remains zero in the shared mask. Reflection, Fresnel, waves, foam and CPU surface sampling consume the same mask; diagnostic 13 displays ownership while 12 retains geometry readback. Six mask/refiner tests and scoped types pass. Matched shaded, body, reflection, Fresnel, foam and ownership captures still show the reported swath after the narrow taper: body color is continuous, while Fresnel response changes strongly across ownership. The final separation and upstream-entry ramps use the local full channel width while preserving the original zero guard and6-meter downstream exit. Matched HIGH-field captures at camera[70,14,5], looking at[25,3.8,20], time20 show the hard green swath replaced by a gradual response. Parent inspection and a reused independent reviewer support this narrow seam repair. Two focused mask tests and scoped types pass, including protected zeros, fully separated interiors, CPU sampling and geometry parity. This is blending two existing surface approximations before shading, not a turbulent mixing model or wider realism acceptance.

Round 31's optional open-strip waterfall remains rejected and disabled: native renders still resemble a uniform white ribbon. A reused critic judged water only against Yosemite footage. A fixed-camera lighting decomposition attributed roughly 86 percent of added water radiance to sky light, but this diagnosis is not a realism fix. Terrain appearance is secondary to the user's water-quality objective.

## Common liquid surface and optical thickness

Verified: 2026-10-06. Round58 follows the completed Pro research direction with an optional shared world-space liquid boundary. Its bounded representation checks pass, but the actual waterfall remains visually rejected. This experiment does not replace the native river or alter Round57 source, motion, flood behavior or arrival ownership. No baked animation is used.

The existing live material feeds waterfallLiquidSurface.ts. Parcel volumes deposit into one normalized field; a fixed half-density contour and the same field's gradients supply geometry and normals. Local covariance may shrink radial ellipsoid axes within a fixed 0.1 m support, never move sample centers or enlarge support to bridge gaps. A conservative upper bound excludes bins that cannot contain the contour, retaining the central-difference normal apron. Below-contour field volume stays accounted for. Mesh volume, deposited material volume and center-density dilution are separate quantities, not interchangeable mass receipts. Capacity failures are explicit and the harness clears stale geometry.

Eight focused tests and scoped types pass. Independent rotated thin-slab quadrature and contour refinement preserve closed outward topology, inputs and the 0.15 m maximum kernel reach. Its resolved thickness approaches 0.12 m: 0.12845, 0.12535 and 0.12333 m. Mesh/material volumes are 96.35%, 96.03% and 97.24%. Earlier rotated-kernel footprint and coarse-grid normal-apron defects were repaired. These controls qualify the surface method at their stated scales, not an arbitrary moving waterfall.

waterfallLiquidSurfaceView.ts uses mesh normals and Float32 ordered depth crossings for liquid thickness. The original HalfFloat additive implementation measured two 1 cm slabs separated by 20 m as only 0.015625 m. The repaired GPU control measures 0.019999988 m. Two separated unit slabs measure 2.000000715 m; half a unit slab hidden by rock measures 0.500196159 m. Eight crossings support four intervals, with a ninth-crossing guard and alternating-face checks. Invalid rays are visibly magenta; the five-layer test correctly fails that guard. The camera must be outside a closed outward mesh with its first entry beyond the near plane. Only the nearest interface supplies reflection/refraction. This is not full multilayer dielectric transport or universal underwater support. Actual shader compilation was checked: expression-returning TSL assignment branches caused invalid WGSL despite passing types, and were changed to block bodies.

At the actual 3 s state, 9,280 material samples carry 1.16 m³. The closed surface has 747,004 triangles and 3,968 disconnected components, with mesh volume 0.4659148 m³ (40.17% of material volume). Deposited volume remains 1.16 m³; 0.6325627 m³ is the integral of field nodes below the contour, not a hidden-material percentage. Center-dilute samples carry 0.31525 m³. Construction took 11.56 s in the measured browser worker and 18.67 s in the independent CPU control; neither is real-time performance. Eleven rendering passes add an unqualified GPU cost.

The browser loaded the complete accepted 3 s solver checkpoint, then calculated the future live to 3.25 s with source history and volume retained. Parent and independent rendered review reject the result: detached short blobs remain in the solid geometry, shaded water is faint and full-height water barely reads. The old sample-rim curls are reduced, but that is not cohesive-water acceptance. Magenta pixels remain in actual water views, exposing unsupported optical rays. This isolated scene does not supply the native river reflection environment. Native rendering source hashes are unchanged; it was not visually requalified by this test.

Next, compare a short downstream region with continued dense simulation using the same physical reconstruction and genuine sample refinement. Measure volume, local density, cross-section, stretch and connectivity to separate transport dilution from underresolved quadrature. Preserve material volume and momentum when adapting samples or carrying finite material deformation. Do not create apparent cohesion with larger kernels or treat numerical blobs as physical breakup. Local air, pool impact, native integration, source restart, remaining rapids realism and real-time cost remain open. The water reference remains Yosemite waterfalls and Merced rapids; terrain beauty is secondary.

Proof: .agent/scratch/waterfall-gauntlet/round58/acceptance.json, round58-water/validation.json and round58-review/report.md. The live isolated harness is round58/live.html. A single parent header sync changes comments only; source and test EOLs are preserved. No broad tests, mining, commits or pushes were performed.

## Live full-height material flow

Verified: 2026-10-06. Round57 completes a live numerical crest-to-bottom control, but rejects its rendered water. The close view shows repeated pale curls around material samples. The full-height view barely reads as water. Native riverWaterfallView.ts and riverWaterMaterial.ts remain outside this change. Terrain appearance is secondary; the water itself must meet the Yosemite and Merced realism reference. No baked animation is used.

WaterfallLiveFlow coordinates the existing bounded crest with WaterfallCrestJetReceiver on the same force clock. Source changes split both phases into identical intervals, including intervals with no crossing packets. A rejected receiver batch stays owned by the coordinator; retry does not advance the crest again or lose drained packets. A receiving plane stores actual arrival time, source ID, birth, volume and vector momentum. It is an arrival boundary, not a pool-impact simulation. Frozen exit transport gradients are retained as measurements, not claimed as full-height deformation.

The longer pulse exposed pressure-support loss after the dense source receded. Two explicit, opt-in reductions keep this material accounted for. Unsupported material strictly beyond the lip can enter the pressure-free receiver without rewriting its velocity. Unsupported upstream material within one grid cell of the bed can enter a separate kinetic residue phase with gravity and contact. Dense water can support its later rejoin; rejoin preserves volume and center momentum but resets unresolved APIC affine. Residue alone cannot rebuild pressure support. Fully dry source restart remains unresolved. Near-bed departure uses the common end of the step, with timing error bounded by the step; normal dense exits keep their swept crossing time. These are reduced models, not proof of physical film dynamics or topological breakup.

The first full-height control also revealed parcels returning into the cliff. An optional swept vertical contact plane now removes the incoming normal velocity and records the rock reaction while retaining tangential motion. It uses free slip and zero normal restitution. Contact is ordered against receiving-plane arrival; an earlier arrival receives no later cliff impulse. Entry through the cliff top remains an explicit unsupported case. Failed queues and contact steps restore state atomically. Invalid earlier runs remain separate evidence rather than being relabeled as repaired runs.

The final fresh control starts with 0.56 m³ at a 70 m crest, adds 1.2 m³/s through a 1 m by 0.7 m opening for 0.5 s, then stops the source. It completes 5 simulated seconds. Initial water first reaches the plane at 3.777880 s; newly injected water first arrives at 4.099094 s. All 9,280 material IDs remain unique: 8,313 arrived, 943 falling and 24 in bed residue. Their volumes are 1.039125, 0.117875 and 0.003 m³, totaling 1.16 m³. The global volume residual is 5.55e-16 m³ and momentum residual magnitude 9.44e-9 kg·m/s. There are 246 cliff contacts and no measured penetration. Those budgets establish ownership and declared force accounting, not physical density or shape convergence.

The browser restored a complete accepted solver state at exactly 2 s, including pressure arrays, source history, affine state, queues and ledgers, then calculated future motion live to 5 s. Its receipts match the independent run. This is checkpoint initialization, not cached animation. Full-height and close views, raw sample positions and console output were inspected. No browser errors or warnings appeared. The unchanged reconstructed-fluid renderer uses fixed 0.065 m sample support in this control; its pale curls and poor distant visibility fail both parent and independent visual review. The simple setting also lacks the native river reflection environment. The native river was not visually replaced or requalified by this isolated test.

All 52 affected tests and six-file scoped types pass. Independent controls cover exact source cuts, retained retry ownership, partial-epoch gravity, bed contact/rejoin, capacity, cliff/arrival ordering and rollback. The fresh run took 318.5 wall seconds for 5 simulated seconds, so this remains far below real time. One parent dependency-header sync updated the three modules; the three tests are outside the dependency graph. Executable output and CRLF were verified unchanged after that comment-only sync.

Next, reconstruct a cohesive, volume-aware liquid surface and derive its normals from that surface, preserving real gaps and thickness. Check silhouette and thickness under sample subdivision before judging the live fall. Do not enlarge kernels merely to disguise sparse samples. Then qualify changing liquid structure, local air, impact and the remaining rapids behavior. Reduced models are allowed; numerical sample particles are not physical droplets. No visual realism acceptance has been awarded.

Proof: .agent/scratch/waterfall-gauntlet/round57/acceptance.json, round57-water/validation.json and round57-review/report.md. The live browser is round57/live.html. These ignored artifacts are disposable; this section is the durable behavior and limitation record. No broad tests, mining, commits or pushes were performed.

## Measured crest transfer into the fall

Verified: 2026-10-06. Round56 qualifies a local transfer from the bounded liquid crest into an isolated thick, pressure-free receiver. It does not change native rendering or complete the water realism goal. The current outlet is about 0.4 m thick by support-based proxies; treating it as an already thin sheet would discard measured geometry.

CrestExit now exports phase, kickStartTime, kickEndTime and remainingDriftTime. Position and time describe the swept boundary crossing; velocity already owns the source interval's complete force kick. WaterfallCrestJetReceiver completes residual drift without applying gravity again, then owns later kicks. It retains parcel ID, source ID, birth, volume, position and vector momentum. Invalid, duplicate, mixed-epoch, out-of-order, capacity and nonfinite batches reject without partial receiver mutation. The caller must process every source-event interval, including empty intervals, and retain drained source packets until receiver acceptance. The two queues are not a single global transaction.

Independent actual crossing controls at three phases and on both sides of a source-event split match uninterrupted uniform freefall at roundoff under the same kick-drift integrator. Eight rejection controls preserve the receiver snapshot. This establishes clock consistency, not exact continuous-time mechanics.

A fresh nominal experiment compares the original outlet at crest minus 2.5 m with a dense domain extended to minus 3.0 m. Both start from the same 0.56 m³ inventory, receive 1.2 m³/s through a 1 m by 0.7 m opening, and stop the source at 0.5 s. At 0.725 s, 875 actual exported parcels match through at most 0.056861 s of receiver ownership. Position RMS is 0.000772 m (maximum 0.002938 m); velocity RMS is 0.010609 m/s (maximum 0.035126 m/s). At fixed 0.1 m reconstruction support, same-query density discrepancy RMS is 0.001376 and maximum absolute discrepancy 0.006049. Still-resident upstream position RMS is 0.00001696 m, showing a small outlet backreaction in this control. Source hashes were frozen throughout the 370-second CPU run. The overlap includes both termination-boundary effects and the difference between source trajectory interpolation and imported momentum velocity. It supports a locally gravity-dominated continuation, not long-term incompressibility, thin conversion, air loading or impact.

Paired side and oblique renders of these recorded states show no obvious transfer seam at this scale. Regular contour ridges remain. The plain blue material is diagnostic and cannot establish realistic water appearance. The measurement inspector is not a baked runtime animation. The original native waterfall renderer hash remains unchanged.

Profiling found repeated per-particle stencil allocations to be a major CPU cost. Equivalent scalar arithmetic removes those temporary arrays and callbacks. Full public snapshots, excluding wall time only, are bitwise identical at every tick in five controls (57 ticks, including actual exits). Two alternating shared-host nominal probes give about 1.98× and 2.14× speedups, but individual 0.0025-second ticks still cost hundreds of milliseconds. These are CPU diagnostics, not native FPS or GPU measurements. Nineteen affected tests and scoped types pass. One parent-owned scoped dependency sync updates only the two module headers; both test files are absent from the dependency graph. Post-test differences are verified as comments only.

The completed Pro consultation and primary author pages support keeping localized liquid dynamics, evolving local air, and explicit differences between dense, thin and dispersed water. [The 2026 two-phase method](https://alexey.stomakhin.com/research/unifluids.html) also acknowledges heuristic breakup and unresolved adaptivity choices in its manuscript; a declared reduced model is permissible if it passes rendered and changing-flow checks. These sources do not establish a browser-ready implementation. Next, extend measured thick parcels through a live full-height visual control, preserve local shape information and source history, and qualify air response and topology changes. Do not force thin admission or demand a full-height dense grid solely because a reduced model is approximate.

Disposable proof and exact hashes are in .agent/scratch/waterfall-gauntlet/round56/acceptance.json, round56-water/validation-final.json and round56-review/report.md. The gallery and GG-384 carry the active checkpoint. No broad tests, memory mining, commits or pushes were performed.

## Dense crest transport and pressure surface

Verified: 2026-10-06. Round 55 repairs the isolated crest experiment in waterfallCrestLiquid.ts. The native riverWaterfallView.ts hash remains 21abb7deb4f1f283758ae28db933cf7dc231e51c2e88b1925ec4c30d835311ed. The new transport and pressure surface are opt-in; this experiment is not wired into the native renderer. No baked animation is used. The full waterfall and rapids realism goal remains open.

Incoming parcels now occupy the actual slab released during their individual ages. The old fixed offset overlapped existing water. Reservoir stencil continuation, free-slip wall support, physical wall contact and tolerant initial quadrature repair the associated inlet error. Short inlet tests pass, but the first repaired candidate worsened late density and was rejected. Preserving summed parcel volume was not sufficient: ordinary quadratic interpolation of a divergence-free MAC field can still compress moving parcels.

The opt-in flux-cell transport uses the six cell-face fluxes to define an RT0 velocity, then integrates its frozen affine trajectory and cell crossings analytically. Quadratic APIC still transports momentum. Shared face-normal velocity preserves the local volume map in the independent manufactured crossing test. This is first-order spatial transport with tangential jumps, and its trajectory differs from the stored APIC velocity. A separate angular-defect ledger reports that approximation. The numerical divergence-free extension supplies dry non-solid support only; it is not an air-pressure or air-mass simulation. The alternative cubic transport still explicitly rejects an incompatible cliff-corner control and has no acceptance here.

Marker-only pressure classification stopped at 0.67 seconds after falsely treating a sealed empty marker cell as air. Independent volume reconstruction at that cell gives a density ratio of 0.918812. The opt-in volume-kernel surface reconstructs the whole pressure boundary consistently at threshold 0.5. Its denominator integrates the geometric non-solid domain, including air, using the quadratic kernel CDF. It never normalizes over the wet mask or patches that one cell. This avoids eroding the wall-side inlet under grid refinement. Raw deposited volume, non-solid deposited volume, corrected-density integral and classified occupied volume remain separate quantities. The fixed physical support has a measured open-corner volume bias of about 0.45–0.49% at 0.05 m grid spacing; it is not exact occupied-volume conservation. Independent closed-head review also found an exact-coordinate wall ghost case, repaired and retested before this checkpoint.

The nominal source-hashed sequence uses a 1 m wide, 0.7 m deep sector with Q=1.2 m³/s, dx=0.1 m, dt=0.0025 s and two samples per cell axis. The source stops at 0.5 seconds. Both the numerical run and live browser reach 0.75 seconds. Resident volume 1.001125 m³ plus 0.158875 m³ of swept exits equals the initial 0.56 m³ plus 0.6 m³ emitted, to about 1.3e-13 m³. The pressure inlet admits 1.2 m³/s before shutoff and zero afterward. Fixed-H=0.1 m parcel-center peak density ratios are 1.068094, 1.208131 and 1.249654 at 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75 seconds; the Round54 baseline gives 1.266167, 1.331082 and 1.361963. Independent reconstruction agrees. These are scale-dependent diagnostics, not full shape convergence. At 0.75 seconds the pressure-classified volume is 0.952 m³ versus 1.001125 m³ of resident material, a 4.9% difference; the displayed smoothed contour is also reported separately. The cumulative angular transport defect is about [-0.508, -0.577, -9.893] kg m²/s and numerical extension impulse about [-113.744, 145.548, 13.850] kg m/s. These measured numerical effects are not physical air loading.

Rendered side views show the crest turning into a descending volume and retained water moving after shutoff. Regular ridges remain, and the blue contour is a geometry diagnostic, not final water shading. CPU quarters took roughly 57–80 seconds on the shared machine; no real-time or GPU performance claim is made. Thin liquid, arbitrary solids, resolved air response, breakup, impact coupling and full-height native rendering remain incomplete. Do not present passing numerical checks as a Yosemite realism pass.

The existing gallery and GG-384 carry the checkpoint. One parent-owned scoped dependency-header sync covers the changed exported module. The relevant recent research is [Jin and Schroeder, divergence-free MAC interpolation over irregular domains (2026)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0021999126002743). ## Dense crest pressure and volume gate

Verified: 2026-10-06. Round 54 rereads Pro's completed recent research and implements an isolated dense crest test in waterfallCrestLiquid.ts. The native water renderer and existing river appearance are unchanged. The complete waterfall and rapids realism goal remains open. No baked animation is used.

The previous full-height test used a 0.7-meter-deep, 1-meter-wide inlet at 1.2 cubic meters per second. Its nominal ballistic centerline starts with a curvature radius of about 0.300 meters. Thickness times curvature is 2.34, violating the thin-sheet assumption; the nominal inner offset surface folds at the lip. A dense liquid region is therefore required before attempting a physical handoff to thin material. A later ballistic estimate is not a substitute for a measured transition from the dense solution.

The bounded prototype uses SI gravity, a staggered liquid pressure grid and quadratic APIC transfers. It reuses the storage, transfer and volume-accounting patterns of the existing worldforge fluid machinery without adopting its tuned compressible Tait pressure. Initial approach water is explicitly booked separately from source inflow. New water retains volume, source identity and birth time. Exported packets retain crossing time, volume and vector momentum; collecting them does not debit water a second time. Source changes affect new inflow, and failed fixed steps restore fields, material and accounting. The current boundary implementation rejects unsupported grid alignment instead of silently changing inlet flux.

Ten focused tests and scoped types pass. Independent controls match hydrostatic pressure to less than 9e-7 pascals, freefall velocity to 2.8e-16 meters per second, and an affine rotation transfer to floating-point precision. Review found and repaired incompatible voxel inlet flux, a bottom-to-top low-flow sampling sweep and failed-step accounting changes. Finite low-flow quadrature bias remains. These are bounded numerical controls, not waterfall appearance acceptance.

The parent rendered the actual repaired source at 0.25 and 0.5 seconds, then stopped inflow and inspected the still-moving water at 0.75 seconds. A world-space density contour and raw material samples expose the computed state using plain diagnostic shading. The 0.1-meter contour support is stated; it is not the preserved river material or a final water surface. The initial browser reload reused a cached bundle, so the final proof uses a versioned script and displays the exact tested source hash. Its first 0.25 seconds of simulation took about 14.4 seconds on this shared machine, far below real time. No isolated GPU or native FPS improvement is claimed.

Volume accuracy remains a separate gate. At 0.25 seconds the visible contour encloses about 0.819 cubic meters while the material ledger holds 0.860; marked voxel volume is 0.936. In a separate low-flow empty-start control, 0.003 cubic meters of material marks 0.040 cubic meters of cells. Marker occupancy includes first-order surface voxelization, so these discrepancies are not all physical compression, but a tiny ledger error or pressure residual cannot establish occupied-volume accuracy. Compare fixed physical fixtures across cell spacing and material quadrature before accepting density, free-surface shape or dense-to-thin transfer. Do not conceal the discrepancy with clipping, inflation or opacity changes.

The independent air study now supplies a continuum regularized response control. A fixed 2-by-2-meter patch, 3-millimeter thickness, 256 material samples, 0.5-meter support radius and 4-meter box give added-air-mass errors of 4.364, 2.265 and 0.124 percent at air spacings 0.25, 0.125 and 0.0625 meters. The independent reference uses a continuum Dirichlet-box Green series. The finest result differs from a uniformly loaded regularized patch by 0.696 percent. Boundary distance and material quadrature were varied separately. Significant pointwise slip remains: this validates an aggregate response, not sharp liquid-air impermeability or the coarse 70-meter falling strip. Its cost and resolution cannot be extrapolated to the full waterfall.

The next gate is dense liquid density and shape convergence, followed by a justified material handoff and physically resolved air response. Wall drainage, arbitrary solid geometry, thin-feature breakup, impact coupling and full-height rendered realism remain incomplete. ## Evolving air projection and the physical resolution gate

Verified: 2026-10-06. Round 53 adds an isolated three-dimensional air-pressure experiment and rejects its full-height result. The latest completed Pro consultation was reread, and the PF-FLIP 2025, multiscale two-phase 2026 and ST-FLIP 2026 author pages were checked directly. Their role remains architectural evidence, not a validated browser implementation. The current native river and waterfall shader are unchanged from round 52. The full realism goal remains open. No baked animation is used.

The strong-flow failure of the previous two-dimensional model has a physical resolution component. For its 3-millimeter sheet and 8-meter-per-second air control, the centerline linear instability peaks at a wavelength of 11.77 millimeters; its short-wavelength cutoff is 5.895 millimeters. At 129 points over 4 meters, point spacing is 31.25 millimeters. Eight intervals per cutoff wavelength would require roughly 5,430 points. The peak also exceeds that model's long-wave thickness assumption. A finite-thickness relation gives a 10.08-millimeter peak instead. Independent finite-matrix eigenmode trajectories match the actual solver to about 1.2e-6 relative error. Initially subdivided and freshly initialized identical material states evolve identically in the short remap control. These checks do not establish breakup physics or remove later remeshing errors; they rule out fixing this regime by late refinement within 129 points alone. The [primary liquid-sheet study](https://www.irphe.fr/~fragmix/publis/VC2002a.pdf) supplies a local laboratory mechanism, not Yosemite calibration.

The new waterfallAirProjection.ts couples liquid normal motion to an evolving staggered air grid. A joint mass-weighted constraint solve handles air divergence and liquid-air exchange. Interpolation and force transfer use exact adjoints; pressure has physical units and open boundaries. Failed projection restores the original state, including air advection in the falling-liquid adapter. Capacity, nonfinite states and unsupported phases are rejected. Separate semi-Lagrangian air transport remains dissipative and is not globally momentum-conservative. This is a regularized immersed response model, not separately resolved pressure on both liquid faces.

The actual 70-meter, 1-meter-wide full-height test at 1.2 cubic meters per second uses 2-meter air cells. Live WebGPU geometry folds into coarse triangles and stops at 3.03 seconds when a vertex leaves the domain. The lowest liquid is still about 38.6 meters above the pool; no water has landed. Volume accounting and equal-and-opposite exchange impulses pass, but the image and trajectory fail. Enlarging the box or adding mist would not validate it. Its old point constraints can erase fine liquid motion absent from the air grid: a three-point normal mode with 3 joules of kinetic energy nearly disappears even with tiny algebraic residuals.

An opt-in material-region coupling repairs this specific overconstraint in a bounded response control. Each caller-owned region constrains area-integrated normal flux. It uses current dual area in both interpolation and its transpose, with no automatic reassignment to world-grid bins. The fine 3-joule mode now survives unchanged. Reports distinguish weak flux residual, mean slip, pointwise slip and physical region span. Separate disconnected layers require separate region IDs. Region span is a diagnostic, not a certificate that the air grid resolves the region.

Sixteen projection tests and nineteen adapter tests pass. Scoped types report zero errors in four files, with none suppressed. A separate dense coupled solve matches velocities within 3.09e-12 meters per second and pressure within 8.17e-11 pascals. A separately assembled dense Poisson calculation checks discrete added-air-mass response across air density and water mass. Coincident equal-area/mass subdivision is invariant. These are discrete consistency checks, not continuum added inertia or general remeshing validation. Translation changes the response by 0.12538 meters per second in the small fixture; finite boundary distance also changes, so this is recorded sensitivity rather than a convergence result.

The full-height adapter intentionally retains point coupling and rejects material-region configuration at construction until it has a justified area/group mapping. The new weak mode has no full-height visual acceptance. Next work must establish a resolved physical pressure response, maintain independent regions for disconnected layers, and define conservative material-area/group transport and a valid dense-to-thin transition. Only then rerun the full-height gate before crest, impact and river integration. Keep existing flood propagation, dry sleeping, source lifetime and optical preservation checks separate from morphology acceptance.

Independent projection and scale evidence is under round53-air/, round53-review/ and .agent/scratch/round53-worker/. Verified: 2026-10-06. Round 50 adds the isolated `waterfallSheetPressure.ts` benchmark. It is a one-dimensional periodic, small-deformation liquid section in the water material frame, with two finite-depth inviscid gas strips and fixed outer walls. A finite-volume Laplace solve provides interface pressure and added gas inertia. Liquid inertia, the pressure difference and the energy of two liquid surfaces advance the material state with implicit midpoint. Gas normal velocity satisfies the linearized interface condition. There is no repeated shape animation or sustained noise input. Thickness remains constant only to first order; large folds, changing thickness, breakup, gravity, a real crest and impact are outside this model. It is not imported into the native river.

The main source direction remains Pro's recent live-water research. The pressure control uses the established normal-velocity and pressure-jump mechanism; [thin-shell fluid coupling](https://graphics.stanford.edu/~erang/papers/thin_shells/thin_shells_fluid_coupling_small.pdf) supplies a numerical coupling reference, not permission to give liquid cloth elasticity. [Liquid-sheet instability theory](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-fluid-mechanics/article/abs/absolute-and-convective-instability-of-a-liquid-sheet/F64636FE7AF169D0FBDCEE918E3B024D) supports the bounded instability control. Displacement stays continuous. Equal-and-opposite interfacial impulse closes to 1.61e-19 pascal seconds in that review fixture. Energy includes each face's gas normal velocity; it is conserved only for the no-shear control. Changing the prescribed base stream is external work, not a solved inlet or a global gas momentum budget. Pressure receipts name their midpoint time and the applied gas speeds, separately from the endpoint state and requested UI speed. Twelve focused tests pass, with zero scoped type errors and zero suppressed imported errors. The source dependency header was synchronized in the parent wave.

Joint sheet/gas refinement from 16 to 32 to 64 to 128 cells reduces displacement error from 5.44 to 1.40 to 0.351 to 0.088 percent; the finest velocity error is 0.125 percent. Independent gas-spacing and timestep sequences show approximately second-order convergence. The timestep reference uses a closed-form lattice response, not the production tridiagonal implementation. The no-shear energy drift is 6.88e-13 relative, and exact zero perturbation stays exactly zero. The validity guard stops at the configured slope/depth limit instead of claiming a nonlinear prediction. They establish state-to-render motion in a linear mechanism test, not realistic waterfall water. The small standalone solver and render-submission timings do not establish native FPS, GPU execution time or a fix to the outstanding first-frame stall. ## Research direction: evolving liquid and secondary whitewater

Verified: 2026-10-05. The owner requested online research into how waterfall water is created. The source review below changes the next implementation priority: stop treating illumination refinement as a sufficient route to realistic falling water. Keep the bounded sky-phase diagnostic available, but prioritize an evolving material surface and its connected secondary effects. This is a working research direction, not an accepted replacement renderer.

### What the references establish

- [Ma et al., experimental free-falling turbulent jet breakup](https://ascelibrary.com/doi/10.1061/%28ASCE%29HY.1943-7900.0001188) report growing disturbances and lateral oscillations during descent, with turbulence and gravity affecting thickness. Only the indexed abstract was accessible; its round-jet observations do not supply a calibrated wide-waterfall breakup law.
- [Ihmsen et al., Unified Spray, Foam and Bubbles](https://cg.informatik.uni-freiburg.de/publications/2012_CGI_sprayFoamBubbles.pdf) separate the triangulated main liquid from secondary water-air material. Their generation criteria and transport connect whitewater to the underlying motion. Their method is approximate and does not establish a browser frame budget.
- [SideFX Whitewater Source](https://www.sidefx.com/docs/houdini/nodes/sop/whitewatersource.html) consumes liquid surface and velocity fields and can source from curvature, acceleration, vorticity, pressure and deformation. [Whitewater Solver](https://www.sidefx.com/docs/houdini/nodes/dop/whitewatersolver.html) separates bubble, foam and spray behavior around the liquid surface. This is an architecture reference, not a plan to depend on Houdini at runtime. The [SOP whitewater workflow](https://www.sidefx.com/docs/houdini/fluid/sopwhitewater.html) explicitly supports fog-volume and mesh output with velocity, and describes density-based erosion to avoid uniform white patches. Secondary material need not appear as visible particle dots. This supports testing connected aerated support with motion-driven formation and fading, rather than simply whitening the coherent sheet.
- [Wretborn et al., Guided Bubbles and Wet Foam](https://www.wetafx.co.nz/assets/Uploads/PDFs/2022-Guided-Bubbles-and-Wet-Foam-for-Realistic-Whitewater-Simulation.pdf) couple bubbles to local liquid behavior and convert rising bubbles into surface foam. Their film-production model is not a demonstrated real-time browser solution.
- [PBRT, Media](https://pbr-book.org/4ed/Volume_Scattering/Media) distinguishes scattering at a dielectric boundary from scattering inside a medium. [NVIDIA, real-time 3D fluids](https://developer.nvidia.com/gpugems/gpugems3/part-v-physics-simulation/chapter-30-real-time-simulation-and-rendering-3d-fluids) describes rendering a liquid boundary from a level set. A particle representation therefore does not require visible particle-shaped water.

### Current implementation mismatch

The optional formation profile in `waterfallDensityAtlas.ts` prescribes descent/emission events, rasterizes filled material strips and globally normalizes each section. It has no independent aeration state driven by local sheet deformation. The actual falling geometry in `riverWaterfallView.ts` follows the separate section envelope. Internal density lobes consequently lack corresponding liquid interfaces and silhouettes. The developed scattering model treats liquid as effective dispersed water with a declared 3 mm interface radius, while preserving clear crest behavior. These are verified code properties; their contribution to perceived ugliness is an inference supported by the rejected native captures, not a measured allocation of error.

At the user's request, ChatGPT Pro researched the problem through the in-app browser and completed after 17 minutes 9 seconds. [The full consultation](https://chatgpt.com/c/6ac42c51-ebdc-83eb-802d-55ce4a6ae7b0) is external advice, not implementation acceptance. The second pass completed after 34 minutes 23 seconds and reviewed 2022-2026 work. Its revised recommendation and independently checked sources appear below. Its initial recommendation is to preserve the shallow-water river and source history, use local three-dimensional liquid dynamics at crest and impact, and evolve sheets, ligaments and droplets as separate material structures through the fall. Screen-space reconstruction remains useful for dense liquid, but cannot create missing topology or weld projected spray into liquid.

Primary sources were checked directly. [Chentanez and Muller](https://matthias-research.github.io/pages/publications/hfFluid.pdf) couple a shallow-water field to noninteracting particles through mass and momentum; this supports mixed representations, not resolved breakup. [APIC](https://disneyanimation.com/publications/the-affine-particle-in-cell-method/) improves particle/grid velocity transfer; it still needs pressure projection, boundaries and interface handling. [Codimensional surface tension flow](https://people.csail.mit.edu/boolzhu/projects/codimension.htm) explicitly represents volumes, sheets, filaments and droplets and their transitions. These papers do not demonstrate this proposed hybrid at Aralia's browser cost or quality target.

The scale check is decisive: a 70-meter gravity fall with a fixed 10-meter-wide, 0.7-meter-deep opening has approximately 3.78 seconds of ideal flight. At Q0.5 and Q12, equivalent unbroken liquid thickness near impact is about 1.35 and 32.3 millimeters respectively. A half-meter isotropic support cannot represent that geometry by enlarging its rounded kernels. Low-flow wetted width must come from crest geometry and drainage; high-flow trajectories must not be forced back into a fixed landing point.

The next bounded implementation gate is a full-height, narrow waterfall experiment with explicit thin-liquid state and a coarse evolving air field. The user explicitly excludes baked animation. Water must respond to arbitrary source histories, retain already released water after shutdown, and exchange volume and vector momentum with one downstream owner. Keep the 70-meter scale and a limited crest sector; simple terrain is sufficient. Compare fixed air, one-way air loading and two-way momentum exchange using identical inflow. Strong interphase drag needs a stable exchange solve, not arbitrary acceleration clipping. This is a proposed reduced model, not an implementation of a published two-phase method.

Track volume, local velocity, material orientation, thickness and connectivity. Stretching changes thickness; breakup transfers volume into rims, ligaments and droplets. The breakup closure remains unvalidated. Its scale must be independent of emission cadence and grid size. Inspect the same state through world-space geometry and screen-space reconstruction, with mist disabled and fixed exposure. Require front/side/orbit consistency, timestep and cadence checks, resolution studies, low/normal/flood inflow, short pulses and shutdown. Source-off accounting alone cannot pass the morphology gate. Only then integrate the actual crest pressure patch, impact/aeration and existing river. Preserve river flooding, dry-cell waking, seam ownership, original optics and the verified underwater repair.

Recent research changes the plan by making water-air feedback explicit. [PF-FLIP (Braun, Bender and Thuerey, 2025)](https://animation.rwth-aachen.de/publication/0594/) demonstrates adaptive two-phase dynamics at workstation/VFX scale. Its showcase reports about two minutes per time step. The released [MSBG code](https://github.com/tum-pbs/MSBG) is grid infrastructure, not the complete liquid solver. [Wretborn, Stomakhin and Batty's 2026 author manuscript](https://alexey.stomakhin.com/research/unifluids.html) couples separated and dispersed phases using phase fractions and interphase forces. The author lists SIGGRAPH Asia 2026; the manuscript carries a December 2026 issue date, so it is forthcoming at this verification date. Direct inspection of Table 3 found 445 large-waterfall frames took 18 hours 41 minutes across three machines. Neither paper establishes browser real-time performance.

[ST-FLIP (2026)](https://ge.in.tum.de/publications/spatiotemporal-flip/) addresses temporal aliasing in particle-grid transfers through space-time sampling. It is a later optimization candidate after morphology and causal timing pass, not a replacement for pressure, collision or breakup. [Manifold death (2022)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.05668) separates a modeled thin-sheet topology-change scale from mesh resolution; it does not supply a universal waterfall rupture threshold. [EA PB-MPM](https://github.com/electronicarts/pbmpm) and [Splash](https://github.com/matsuoka-601/Splash) are directly relevant WebGPU engineering references, not accepted waterfall implementations. No verified recent result removes the combined browser cost, thin-feature dynamics and arbitrary-inflow challenges.

The consultation also reviewed recent interface tracking, kinetic free-surface solvers, coupled bubbles/foam, transparency and learned models. Those remain research leads until their primary methods and implementation costs are checked for the intended prototype. Online neural fitting, reduced training-space dynamics and rendered playback must not be mistaken for a solver that meets the user's arbitrary live source contract. The next change should improve evolving liquid structure; another smoothing or mist pass over the rejected strip is not the next gate.
